items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Benny Goodman came up, by then Krupa and Harry James had left him but he had Nick Fatool on drums and Fletcher Henderson was playing piano.

ctx.x: Yes, something like that. And Charlie Barnet’s band, I got to see them. As a matter of fact, Charlie Barnet, he was out here in 1939. So I guess he did a picture then. Because he played the old Palomar, before the Palladium in Los Angeles. And so the Palomar had Charlie Barnet, and see they used to broadcast and I would listen to them on the radio. Artie Shaw’s band was there, Buddy Rich was with him — I would listen to them, then Barnet’s band. Now Barnet, his closing night, he closed and Count Basie was…

perform at our Exposition. They were at Exposition 1939 World Exposition at Treasure Island. And I was blessed because I was in it all night. I got to go there and see that. Benny Goodman came up, by then Krupa and Harry James had left him but he had Nick Fatool on drums and Fletcher Henderson was playing piano. And that was a kind of memorable because our show was at the Golden Gate Theater. And Goodman was at Treasure Island. So that meant you taxied between the two. And I don’t know how we did it because we…
Juggling and all that kind of stuff.
